target: connective (PO_0009068): a cardinal organ part (PO_0025001) part_of connective, i.e. a lobe of the connective (part of a qualified whole)
reason: Lobes or appendages of the anther connective (e.g. Melastomataceae). The organ is named, so unlike the generic 'lateral lobe' it can be expressed as a lobe part of PO connective. One flora only, so no separate class.
Unit of density (count per square cm), not a structure. As in the earlier 'per node' and 'per cell' items.
Narrower: hairs on a (fern) rhizome. PO has 'hair' as a synonym of trichome, and the whole is named.

label: spadix staminate zone
parent: is_a PO_0009011 plant structure; part_of PO_0030120 spadix inflorescence
definition: A plant structure (PO:0009011) that is the portion of a spadix inflorescence (PO:0030120) bearing the staminate flowers. NOTE: Sibling of spadix appendix (FLOPO_0986049); PO has no classes for the zones of a spadix. Propose to PO together with the appendix and a pistillate zone.
reason: Araceae treatments describe the length, diameter and colour of the male zone itself, not of its flowers, so 'staminate flower part_of spadix' would misplace the length. The earlier review already noted that PO has no spadix zones.

target: plant-type cell wall (GO:0009505) part_of plant cell (PO_0009002) part_of cortex (PO_0005708)
reason: Walls of cortical cells, e.g. in Sphagnum stem cortex descriptions. Expressible as a chain of existing GO and PO classes, so no new class is needed.
Margin of a leaf lamina lobe. Lobe class exists; margin is a standard region.

target: spike inflorescence (PO_0030117) with basal (FLOPO_0991002) as bearer quality
reason: Narrower: spikes arising at the plant base (Cyperaceae). 'basal' is already a bearer_quality context word; add 'spike' to its list of qualified heads in flora_context_words.tsv. The count goes on the spike.
Fragment of a count ('up to 4 above midrib'). The counted structure is not named, and the midrib is only a position (leaf midvein PO_0020139).
Narrower: a labellum lobe that is part of the hypochile (FLOPO_0986030); can add part_of hypochile.
The disc of an orchid lip is its central upper surface bearing calli, papillae or hairs. A region of an existing FLOPO class, not the floral disc (FLOPO_0986025).

target: stomatal complex (PO_0002000) part_of leaf epidermis (PO_0006016) (abaxial/adaxial via surface context), with present (PATO_0000467)
reason: Lines are rows of stomata on conifer leaves. The bearer is the stomatal complex; 'present' is the quality fused into the name.

label: perianth limb
parent: is_a PO_0025269 collective organ part structure; part_of PO_0009058 perianth
definition: A collective organ part structure (PO:0025269) composed of the expanded distal portions of the tepals, sepals or petals of a fused perianth (PO:0009058), above the perianth tube. NOTE: Complements perianth tube (FLOPO_0986010) and perianth lobe (FLOPO_0986004); modelled on corolla limb (FLOPO_0986012). Propose to PO with perianth tube.
reason: Perigone = perianth (earlier review). FLOPO has perianth tube and lobe but no limb. The limb is used widely (Aristolochiaceae, Thymelaeaceae, Nyctaginaceae, monocots).
Margin of the receptacle. In Dorstenia-like floras this is an inflorescence receptacle, which PO lacks, so mapping to PO_0009064 is approximate.
Narrower: ramenta are thin multicellular epidermal scales or hairs of ferns and mosses. PO trichome already covers scale, lepis and squama.
Count fragment ('1–8 in each row'); the counted structure is elsewhere. As 'per whorl'.
Exact; hyphenated form of 'stem leave', already mapped to cauline leaf in the earlier review.
Unclear without the organ (stem joints, pinna joints, leaf joints?). The earlier review also rejected 'articulation'.
The lamina of an Asteraceae ray floret is the expanded limb of its corolla. Not PO ligule (PO_0020105), which is the grass leaf ligule.
Generic side of a fern pinna or pinnule. It needs the organ it belongs to, as with 'margin'. Better as a context word (basiscopic/acroscopic, like abaxial) than as a bearer.
Count phrase; the counted part is the leaf (vascular leaf PO_0009025, blade = leaf lamina PO_0020039) and 'per whorl' is the count frame. As 'per whorl'.
Narrower: a nectary sunk in a pit. Its shape (open, rounded, emarginate) is a quality of the nectary.
A quality word; the part in the examples is papilla (papilla cell PO_0025166, per the earlier review).
Narrower: first-order (outer) involucral bracts, e.g. subtending the primary rays of a pseudumbel. 'Primary' is a position in a series.

label: pseudocephalium
parent: is_a PO_0009011 plant structure; part_of PO_0009047 stem
definition: A plant structure (PO:0009011) that is a flowering zone of a cactus stem (PO:0009047) whose areoles bear dense wool or bristles, without the marked change in stem anatomy of a true cephalium. NOTE: PO has neither cephalium nor pseudocephalium; propose both to PO together.
reason: A real Cactaceae structure that is counted ('Pseudocephalia 1-3'), so it needs a class. Only one flora here, so low priority.
Narrower: in Ophioglossaceae the sporophore is the fertile, sporangium-bearing segment of the leaf. Do not use the fungal sense (fruit body).
Ratio fragment ('2 × as long as ovary'). Handled by pattern 10 (ratio to another part) with ovary as the other part.

target: rostellum (FLOPO_0986017): a cardinal organ part (PO_0025001) part_of rostellum
reason: Lobes of the orchid rostellum. The whole exists as a FLOPO class; the lobe is a part of a qualified whole.
Small tooth; a generic part that needs the organ it belongs to (leaf, calyx, appendage...).
Narrower: an inflorescence bract part_of spike inflorescence (PO_0030117).
An absence statement: bract (PO_0009055) with absent (PATO_0000462), 'lateral' as position. Not a structure name.
